title: Fuel delivery, pressure, volume and injector balance
whatItIs: The fuel system must deliver the commanded fuel mass at the exact load and RPM where torque is requested. Pressure at idle alone is not enough; volume and voltage under load matter.
normalValues: Closed-loop trims should stay near zero in normal cruise. Under heavy load, commanded lambda and measured response must stay plausible and the engine should not go lean when airflow rises.
deviations: Positive trims mainly under load suggest fuel volume, pump voltage, filter or injector flow limitation
Negative trims and fuel smell suggest overfueling, leaking injector, high pressure or purge vapor
One-cylinder misfire with trim disturbance can be injector imbalance
Normal idle pressure with lean WOT can still be a weak pump volume fault
influence: Fuel delivery faults can damage the engine under load through lean combustion and knock, so load-only lean patterns are high priority.
checks: Measure pressure and volume under load
Check pump voltage drop and ground
Run injector balance or cylinder contribution tests when one cylinder/bank is suspicious
